quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the person in charge of the whole school!
quests.question: Principal
quests.hint: This person leads the whole school, not just one classroom.
quests.explanation: Yes! A principal is the person who leads and takes care of the whole school.
quests.funFact: A principal often visits many classrooms in just one single school day!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the person who takes care of the library!
quests.question: Librarian
quests.hint: This person knows exactly where every book belongs on its shelf.
quests.explanation: Yes! A librarian takes care of the library and helps us find books.
quests.funFact: A librarian often knows hundreds of book titles and where each one belongs!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the big yellow vehicle that takes us to school!
quests.question: School Bus
quests.hint: It is big, often yellow, and has many seats inside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A school bus is the big vehicle that carries students to and from school.
quests.funFact: School buses are often painted bright yellow so drivers can spot them easily!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the outdoor place where we play and swing!
quests.question: Playground
quests.hint: This is an outdoor spot with slides, swings, and lots of running.
quests.explanation: Yes! A playground is the outdoor place where we play during recess.
quests.funFact: Many playgrounds have slides, swings, and climbing bars all in one place!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the room where students eat their lunch!
quests.question: Cafeteria
quests.hint: This big room has many tables where students sit to eat.
quests.explanation: Yes! A cafeteria is the room where students sit down to eat lunch.
quests.funFact: Some school cafeterias can serve lunch to hundreds of hungry students every day!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for a friend who learns in your class with you!
quests.question: Classmate
quests.hint: This person sits near you and learns in the very same class.
quests.explanation: Yes! A classmate is another student who learns in your class with you.
quests.funFact: Working with a classmate on a project is a great way to learn together!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the helper who finds you a good book to read!
quests.question: Librarian
quests.hint: You can ask this person to help you find a good book.
quests.explanation: That's right! A librarian can help you pick a great book to read.
quests.funFact: A librarian often knows hundreds of book titles and where each one belongs!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the quiet room filled with rows of books!
quests.question: Library
quests.hint: This room is filled with shelf after shelf of books to borrow.
quests.explanation: Yes! A library is a quiet room full of books we can borrow and read.
quests.funFact: A library can hold thousands of books for students to borrow and enjoy!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the leader who helps every teacher and student!
quests.question: Principal
quests.hint: This person's office often welcomes visitors who come to the school.
quests.explanation: That's right! A principal helps every teacher and student in the school.
quests.funFact: A principal often visits many classrooms in just one single school day!

quests.instruction: Find the word for another student who sits and learns beside you!
quests.question: Classmate
quests.hint: You might sit next to this person or share a table with them.
quests.explanation: That's right! A classmate shares lessons, games, and school days with you.
quests.funFact: Working with a classmate on a project is a great way to learn together!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the vehicle that picks up students every morning!
quests.question: School Bus
quests.hint: It stops along a route each morning to pick up students.
quests.explanation: That's right! We ride a school bus to get to school safely.
quests.funFact: School buses are often painted bright yellow so drivers can spot them easily!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the place with slides and swings at school!
quests.question: Playground
quests.hint: You visit this place during recess to play with your friends.
quests.explanation: That's right! We run, swing, and slide at the playground.
quests.funFact: Many playgrounds have slides, swings, and climbing bars all in one place!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the place where we borrow books to read!
quests.question: Library
quests.hint: You must stay quiet here so everyone can read in peace.
quests.explanation: That's right! We visit a library to find a new book to read.
quests.funFact: A library can hold thousands of books for students to borrow and enjoy!

quests.instruction: Touch the thin sheet a pencil or crayon can leave a mark on!
quests.question: Paper
quests.hint: It is thin, flat, and usually white or another light color.
quests.explanation: Yes! Paper is the flat sheet we write, draw, and color on.
quests.funFact: Paper was first made from tree bark, plants, and old cloth long ago!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the big room full of tables where we eat!
quests.question: Cafeteria
quests.hint: You carry your lunch tray here when it's time to eat.
quests.explanation: That's right! We carry our lunch trays into the cafeteria to eat.
quests.funFact: Some school cafeterias can serve lunch to hundreds of hungry students every day!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the place where lunch trays are carried to a table!
quests.question: Cafeteria
quests.hint: This big room has many tables where students sit to eat.
quests.explanation: Well done! A cafeteria has plenty of tables for the whole school to eat together.
quests.funFact: Some school cafeterias can serve lunch to hundreds of hungry students every day!

quests.instruction: Touch the small stick that writes in white or color on a board!
quests.question: Chalk
quests.hint: It feels a little dusty and can leave marks on your fingers.
quests.explanation: That's right! Chalk leaves a soft mark that a cloth can wipe away.
quests.funFact: Chalk is made from a soft rock that can be ground into a stick!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the room where we whisper quietly among the books!
quests.question: Library
quests.hint: This room is filled with shelf after shelf of books to borrow.
quests.explanation: Well done! A library keeps rows and rows of books for everyone to enjoy.
quests.funFact: A library can hold thousands of books for students to borrow and enjoy!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the person who keeps every book on its shelf!
quests.question: Librarian
quests.hint: This person knows exactly where every book belongs on its shelf.
quests.explanation: Well done! A librarian keeps every book organized and easy to find.
quests.funFact: A librarian often knows hundreds of book titles and where each one belongs!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the fun outdoor spot we visit during recess!
quests.question: Playground
quests.hint: This is an outdoor spot with slides, swings, and lots of running.
quests.explanation: Well done! A playground gives students a fun place to play outside.
quests.funFact: Many playgrounds have slides, swings, and climbing bars all in one place!

quests.instruction: Touch the colorful liquid we spread on paper with a brush!
quests.question: Paint
quests.hint: You need a brush to spread it smoothly across your page.
quests.explanation: That's right! We dip a brush in paint to color a picture.
quests.funFact: Paint dries as the water inside it slowly disappears into the air!

quests.instruction: Touch the container we fill with water to drink during the school day!
quests.question: Water Bottle
quests.hint: You take small sips from it when you feel thirsty.
quests.explanation: That's right! We sip from a water bottle to stay refreshed at school.
quests.funFact: Drinking enough water can help your brain stay focused during class!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the person whose office helps run the whole school!
quests.question: Principal
quests.hint: This person leads the whole school, not just one classroom.
quests.explanation: Well done! A principal makes sure the whole school runs smoothly.
quests.funFact: A principal often visits many classrooms in just one single school day!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the vehicle with rows of seats that drives us home!
quests.question: School Bus
quests.hint: It is big, often yellow, and has many seats inside.
quests.explanation: Well done! A school bus has room for many students to ride together.
quests.funFact: School buses are often painted bright yellow so drivers can spot them easily!

quests.instruction: Touch the sticky roll we use to join paper or fix a torn page!
quests.question: Tape
quests.hint: You peel a strip off and press it down to make things stick.
quests.explanation: That's right! We peel off a strip of tape to fix or stick things.
quests.funFact: Sticky tape lets people join paper together without any glue mess!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the vehicle that stops at your street every school morning!
quests.question: School Bus
quests.hint: It stops along a route each morning to pick up students.
quests.explanation: Yes! A school bus is the big vehicle that carries students to and from school.
quests.funFact: School buses are often painted bright yellow so drivers can spot them easily!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for a friend who shares your classroom every day!
quests.question: Classmate
quests.hint: This person sits near you and learns in the very same class.
quests.explanation: Well done! A classmate can become a great friend during the school year.
quests.funFact: Working with a classmate on a project is a great way to learn together!

quests.instruction: Find the item we slide our worksheets inside to keep them safe!
quests.question: Folder
quests.hint: It keeps your worksheets flat and safe inside your backpack.
quests.explanation: Well done! A folder protects our papers on the way to and from school.
quests.funFact: Colorful folders can help students quickly find the right subject for each class!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool with two blades that we use to cut paper!
quests.question: Scissors
quests.hint: It is always used slowly and carefully, with an adult nearby to help.
quests.explanation: Yes! Scissors have two blades that we use to cut paper carefully.
quests.funFact: The very first scissors were shaped very differently from the ones we use today!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool a student uses first to practice writing letters!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: It often has an eraser sitting right on top of it!
quests.explanation: That's right! We hold a pencil to make letters and pictures on paper.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people wrote with sticks and feathers before pencils were invented!
